Review Title: Right side rewards, left side regrets.
Review Text: This sightseeing flight offered some beautiful views, but I found the experience heavily favored passengers on the right side of the aircraft. As a left-side passenger, my view was primarily of the shoreline, and I missed out on many of the central island's key attractions like the mountains, canyons, and waterfalls. To maximize your experience, I'd strongly recommend requesting a right-side seat. Additionally, strategically maneuvering the aircraft to provide brief, alternating views of key landmarks for both sides of the plane could help ensure a more equitable experience for all passengers.

Review Title: Great value, awesome pilot and wonderful views
Review Text:
I had been looking at this flight since we began planning our trip to Kauai, but was still on the fence . We did a helicopter tour of the Big Island 20 years ago and kept wondering if it was worth double the price to go on a helicopter here. On our first day we drove out to Waimea Canyon and there we made our choice. We saw the plane and a helicopter pass over us and decided the plane looked great.

We booked the flight online 10:30 am (later we heard a pilot share this was the best time but honestly I don't think you could go wrong either time. )

Got to the airport and checked in a little later our pilot Nick came by and welcomed us. Walked out to the plane did a little safety brief, low door watch your head and so on, then loaded the plane for the typical over the water flight, loved the bit of humor with the air sickness bag and taxid out to the runway.
Nick is a wonderful young pilot, those folks seem to be getting younger every year, or .aybe it's just me. Local guy, no doubt loves what he does and where he lives. Offered a great tour pointing out highlights and the coolest thing was making some left hand turns for those of us on the other side of the plane. Great pilot he banked us over so we could get some great pictures and did it so SMOOTHLY that we hardly noticed.
We took some incredible pictures and a few videos of the entire island. It was really cool having him point out places we had visited and see it from the air.
Wish there was a higher rating we could give. Highly recommend this trip 👌 best value and awesome views, what a combo!
Use my name when you get there they won't remember me just say little round guy big smile, grinned the rest of the day. Book it book it now
. Can't wait to come back and do it again.

Review Text:
This may very well be the most beautiful place I have ever visited. We were in Oahu for one week and then Kauai. Why did we not just go to Kauai for two weeks?
We had a small condo in Kapaa in the Coconut Beach area and that is where we will stay when we come again. I like the area and it is pretty easy to get everywhere from there. There is a park nearby called Lydgate Park that would be great to take kids to or anyone leery of ocean swimming as it has 2 areas blocked off by big boulders so that there is no worry about getting in too deep or being knocked down by waves. It also has a huge playground.
We initially were holding a very expensive rental car but I kept checking and got it down to a reasonable amount. There is no charge to park anywhere we went.
Be prepared for bad roads if you go the scenic route. Many of the scenic roads are rutted and have potholes the size of a VW bug. When it rains on Kauai (it rains a lot), there are red mud puddles in areas that you will go to sightsee. If you plan to hike, take it seriously. Many of the hikes are considered to be for those more experienced hikers and you will need real hiking shoes. Also plan on slippery areas on the hike so a fall in the mud is possible.
The rest of the island has good roads and no mud so you don’t have to engage with the mud if you don’t want to.
We paid for an app called the Shaka guide. They offer 4 GPS tours which covers the whole island and is definitely worth the money!
This island has a slower pace than Oahu but you can still get into traffic in the morning and evening drive time if you are around Lihue.
The airport is adorable and very easy to get around. Don’t be surprised to find chickens near the luggage carousel. i read that Kauai has about 75,000 people and 450,000 chickens. Therefore don’t expect to sleep much past sunrise due to the roosters crowing. But then who would want to miss a sunrise in Kauai anyway?

Review Text:
I was on the island of Oahu, Hawaii when my plans to visit Pearl Harbor fell through.  I didn’t want to waste one day of our two week vacation and so I decided to research how I could visit Kauai for one day. You may think that is a ridiculous idea however, once I found Air Ventures Hawaii and spoke to a representative early Wednesday morning to secure the proper flight times for Thursday I decided to book a flight to Lihue via Southwest.  We arrived at noon and our Air Ventures flight was booked for 1:30pm.  The cost was $337.08 (two passengers) for one hour.  This flight was definitely longer, less expensive, and more beautiful than our helicopter tour that we took a few days prior to this adventure.  Trisha and her assistant greeted us with a warm Aloha and they were extremely professional and helpful.  I am happy that they informed us about paying $30.00 to capture the GoPro footage of our one hour flight.  The footage from the NaPali Coast was unbelievable yet stunning! It is well worth the money.  
Prior to boarding we were weighed and seated in a nice open air waiting room.  I would suggest that a few hours prior to the flight that you take Dramamine to ensure you will not experience any motion sickness.  I always practiced this so I didn’t have any problems on the flight.  I believe only one passenger was somewhat ill.  I think this is important because the flight is absolutely breathtaking and you simply don’t want to be ill while enjoying such an unimaginable view.  Please be mindful that Air Ventures Hawaii has no control over Mother Nature and sometimes a few bumps might occur throughout the flight.  
Nate was our pilot. I must admit that this guy was stellar!!!  First, he has the best personality.  He welcomed us aboard as guests, explained all safety precautions, told us exactly what would happen while in flight, and even explained what we would see while on the trip.  In addition, he was a skilled aviator that paid attention to the details of safety and also provided valuable information at the same time.  I am very happy that Air Ventures Hawaii takes passenger safety seriously.  
In addition to being a good aviator the pilot did an excellent job of explaining all the different sights that we saw during the flight.  I must admit that I love seeing the Grand Canyon of the Pacific and the waterfalls however, the NaPali Coast is a sight to behold.  Nate indicated that the NaPali Coast is considered one of the most beautiful coastlines in the world.  I agree with him unequivocally!! My eyes have not seen such natural uninhabited beauty like that since visiting Bora Bora in 2007.  The beauty of the NaPali Coast is the best reason to take this flight.  In addition, if you can only spend a day on the island it will take two hours to reach the NaPali Coast and I believe much of it cannot be reached by foot.  I believe seeing the coastline from the air is unexplainable in words and unimaginable even when you see it.  Bucket list for sure!!!!!
Our day trip to Kauai was stellar because my son and I had an opportunity to see all of the natural beauty of Kauai from the sky.  If you are in search of seeing unexplainable and breathtaking beauty I would suggest Air Ventures Hawaii.  Nate was an exceptional pilot and I feel I received everything that I paid for and more.  Thanks Nate for being a wonderful host and helping my son and I make beautiful memories.  We will forever remember the time we spent over the NaPali Coast because of you!  Mahalo for everything!!!! You represent Air Ventures Hawaii well!!! Keep up the great work!

Review Text:
Vielleicht ist es wichtig zu sagen, dass viele der atemberaubenden Landschaften auf Kauai lediglich per Boot oder gar nicht zugänglich sind. Das erklärt, warum Kauai so paradiesisch ist… Denn hier kann die Natur in freien Bahnen wachsen und gedeihen.

Da ich (fast) alleine reiste und beim besten Willen nicht alles zu Fuß oder Auto hätte sehen können, entschied ich mich für diese Tour.

Allen Liebhaber außergewöhnlicher Landschaften und der Natur insgesamt kann ich diesen Flug nur empfehlen. Hier ein paar Punkte, die mir wichtig waren und erfüllt bzw. übertroffen wurden:

TOUR: In der Tat handelt es sich um eine KOMPLETTE Tour. Wir umrundeten die Insel und haben alles gesehen, was in jedem Reiseführer empfohlen wird (wahrscheinlich) auch noch mehr.

FÜR ALLE: da ich allein war, durfte ich mich auf Nachfrage einfach neben den Piloten hinsetzen. Was natürlich mega war. Besonders charmant fand ich, dass der Pilot immer gedreht hat, damit nicht nur die Passagieren an der rechten sondern auch an der linken Seite alles sehen konnten.
Das habe ich selten bei vorherigen Rundflügen erlebt.

SICHERHEIT: Von der Buchung bis zur Durchführung hatte ich stets den Eindruck, dass das gesamte Personal an alles gedacht hat. Die Machine war sauber und flog problemlos, der Pilot hatte neben den üblichen Elementen auch ein iPad am Board und ging damit und mit dem Flugzeit selbstverständlich um.
Bevor wir einstiegen wurde unseren Impf/Teststatus erneut geprüft.

PILOT: Unser Pilot Nate ist extrem erfahren, ortskundig und sehr professionell. Die Kombi hat es möglich gemacht, dass er neben der kurzen und verständlichen Erklärungen auch Zeit für Witze gefunden hat.

PREIS-LEISTUNGSVERHÄLTNIS: Einfach Top. Wer schon mal in Deutschland einen Rundflug gemacht hat, weißt, dass 30-45 Minuten schon mal 170€ kosten können.
Für 130€ haben wir die ganze Insel gesehen, super Erklärungen und Insights bekommen, waren über 70 Minuten in der Luft und hatten eine butterweiche Landung. Mehr geht echt nicht.

Die Krönung für mich war, dass ich danach gefragt habe, ob Jill (die super nette Amerikanerin an der Rezeption für mich ein Taxi rufen konnte). Nach ein paar Minuten kam Jill mit Ray (einem anderen Piloten), der mich gefragt hat, ob er mich zum Hotel fahren dürfte, da er 3 Stunden bis zur nächsten Tour frei hat. Ist das nicht traumhaft??? :)
Ray war über 40 Jahre Pilot bei einer amerikanischen Airline und setzte sich mit seiner Frau vor 20 Jahren hier ab. Es war super nett, bei ihm mitfahren zu dürfen und so viele coole Geschichten zu hören!

Es war tatsächlich der schönste Rundflug, den ich in meinem Leben gemacht habe.

Und für diesen Paradies würde ich die Tour als ein MUSS empfehlen.

Review Text:
This is my second time taking the Island Air Tour; this time we brought friends with us. To say that we had a memorable experience is an understatement. The scenery from the air was breathtaking; everything from the Poipu Coast, Waimea Canyon, the amazing waterfalls, Hanalei Bay and the Islands beauty. My favorite remains the Napali Coastline in all it's magnificent splendor; it truly is Bali Hai.

Ten years ago we flew with Ray Smith, a 34 year veteran flying Jumbo Jets for United Airlines. Since then, Ray bought the company and still loves sharing this beautiful Island with all his guest. Our pilot today was Nate who was not only friendly but very knowledgeable in sharing with us so much about Kauai that we had never heard on any other tour during our several visits to Kauai. Nate also was more than willing to fly back over parts of the Island that we wanted to see up close again. Even though this is the middle of November with unpredictable weather we had beautiful sunshine and even the highest point on Kauai was fully visible.

The plane itself is unique, built in Australia to use by Bush pilots, the aircraft is steady and able to cruise much slower than the Helicopters that you can tour with on the Island. The interior of the aircraft was comfortable even for me who is 6'1" and 230 lbs. In fact I got to sit in the Co-Pilots seat! Each seat however has a bubble window which gives excellent visibility and is perfect for your camera or I phone for picture taking. Every guest has a headphone which keeps you in contact with the pilot and all the other guest. The headphones also filter out excess engine noise which enables everyone to carry on a pleasant conversation and to ask any question they wish about the Island.

Ray and his wife are truly customer oriented in answering questions and making this a great experience from beginning to end.

We love coming to Kauai to go swimming on the amazing beaches; riding bicycles; go on Snorkeling and Dinner Cruises; tubing in the sugar cane canals; and of course the Luaus. All of these are fun and have produced lasting memories with our children and now our grandchildren. Having done all of this over the years I can honestly say, If there is only 1 tour that you must take on Kauai, Air Adventures is that tour.

Review Text: Flying open air, low and slow is absolutely the best way to see Kauai. My wife and I drove the entire island and would have missed most of its beauty.as much of it is inaccessible. My wife is a bit of a nervous flier in small planes and the team at Air Ventures put her at ease all along the way - from the pre-flight briefing to a super smooth landing and the entire comfortable flight in-between. Most of the flight was flown at approx. 1,800-2,500 feet and between 80-90 kts. It was amazing how much we could see, how good the view was for both of us sitting side-by-side with our pilot in the cockpit behind us and with the high-end headsets we were provided our pilot gave us great information on what we were seeing, history and etc. We've been on helicopter tours and given they seat 4-6 people always get stuck in the middle and miss the best sight seeing... Review Text: Even before we boarded AirVenture's Cessna Skylane for our private tour of the island, Jill's cheerful greeting & bubbly demeanor welcomed us as we arrived at the hangar. (Air Ventures also offers add-on options to record your flight.)  Although cloud-less skies are rare here, Ray maximized our time aloft by adjusting his course enroute to ensure  we had clear visibility & spectacular views.  His knowledge about the history of the island meshed nicely with the waypoints along the tour & the amount of narrative never overwhelmed our sense of awe at what we were seeing. I'm so glad opted to fly with Air Ventures instead of booking a helicopter tour.  Besides being much less expensive, the pace of the flight was more leisurely; we had time to identify & focus on points of interest as Ray pointed them out.  We saw a lot of helicopters flying around us during the tour & they looked frenetic & fast paced - I didn't see them hover for very long at any one place.   The price of our flight, the added value of the warm & welcoming staff & the quality of Ray's excellent airmanship & piloting skills made this an experience we would highly recommend for everyone! Review Text:
Short version: amateur, unprofessional, overpriced, uncomfortable, rude, terrible experience. Spend the extra money and take a he'll ride, or at least use a different plane ride provider!

Long version: We arrived at 925 for our 10am departure, and after the counter employees spent ten minutes in what seemed like some kind of candid camera routine, they informed us that there was some kind of "system error" leaving us as the only two passengers for the flight, which they "couldn't do." They told us we had to come back at 11.
We returned at 11 and waited over an hour before we finally got in the air with a pilot who clearly had very little experience flying or in customer service. After informing us he "wasn't supposed to be here today" and that the pilots don't even get paid, and that one of these tour planes had just crash landed the other day, we proceeded on our unprofessional and abbreviated tour of the island. After learning we were newlyweds he informed us that he was thinking of getting engaged so he could stop using condoms but that he had been a man whose so his girl wamts him to use them. This was one of the few statements he made that didn't begin with "I'm not supposed to tell you this, but..."
I know that they cannot be held accountable for inclement weather but we deliberately booked the earliest flight available to get out before the weather turned. About the time the 10am flight landed the storm moved in and we were unable to see much of anything on our flight.

Had we been on the flight we booked (both airbusses flew at 10am, despite the story that there were only two of us booked) we might have an entirely different review.
Had they just admitted it was their mistake we might have an entirely different review.
Had they just been honest before takeoff that due to weather we would not be able to see the napali coast, we might have an entirely different review.

But the unprofessional pilot and the unprofessional gate staff and the unprofessional business model of this place left us wishing we had spent the extra money and taken a helicopter ride instead of what now feels like a tourist trap rip-off. Cannot even shrug this off as a "you get what you pay for" experience, as we paid for a 10am professionally piloted all-island tour. And got a short plane ride with a kid who didn't want to be there, and frankly, shouldn't have.

Review Text:
We did this Tour on May 21st 2019. Initially, I was looking for helicopter tours but on discovering that they assign seats based on height and weight and that the helicopter has “middle seats” I decided to look into Air ventures. I am glad I did.
First off, there are no middle seats; everyone gets a window. I had booked the morning tour, but due to unforeseen circumstances, the tour had to be moved to the afternoon. They were kind enough to inform me 1 day before the trip. The change was done free of charge. If we could not make it, they were willing to rebook us on a different day that would work out. If we could not attend, I am sure they would have refunded us.
We had 4 people in total who took the same plane ride with us, so we all sat on the same side, but had there been more our pilot Justin T (not Timberlake! ) would have maneuvered the plane so all could get a good look.
The view of the NaPali coast from air was breathtaking. Justin also played some mild background music while he narrated the history of Kauai and pointed out interesting features. For me seeing the NaPali coast and the beautiful reefs from the sky was like the scene from Avatar where the protagonist sees the Floating Mountains of Pandora for the first time. Magnificent. We also saw the Waimea canyon (also known as Grand Canyon of the Pacific). It was lush green and had countless waterfalls. Justin was kind enough to fly the plane around slowly and more than once so we could truly take in the beauty. I was lucky enough to get to sit in the co-pilot’s seat, but all the seats are good. Do make sure you wear all black clothes, else your reflection will show up in the window and ruin your photos. The windows are large enough that you get a good view and squeaky clean too. Side note: Do not put your phone on the windowsill while recording, the vibration though not obvious when flying, will show up on your videos prominently.

Before we began our trip, they also took a photo of all of us and the pilot together and emailed it to us at no extra charge.
For an extra charge of $25, they will attach your GoPro to the exterior of the plane, just below the wing and you can get an uninterrupted video of the whole trip. We did purchase this, and it was completely worth it. You get to relive the experience all over again.

P.S: Ground Staff Jill was super helpful and friendly too. She mentioned must see places and helped us pick out nice restaurants for us to visit.

TLDR; Awesome experience. An absolute must do. Staff were very courteous, fun and informative.

Review Text:
Amazing views of the island with a safety reassuring pilot.
Located at the end of the airport terminal, with free parking. Quick and easy check in process. Very quick boarding process and takeoff procedure to see the views of the island, narrated by the pilot.
Saw most parts of the island, doing a few 360 turns, to let all passengers view some attractions from all directions and both sides.

For professional or 'prosumers' photographers, be aware that while the windows are large and clean, reflection from them do creep up to the photos. Bring a wide lens. A telephoto lens will be hard to use/not useful. Try to block some reflections e.g. with your hand. For all other amateurs, bringing a good camera phone is sufficient :-)
Consider enjoying the ride instead of taking too many photos.

The seats on the plane are low but otherwise comfortable. The flight felt safe and not at all scary or bumpy (though weather might impact your ride). I brought with me a water bottle and large camera with no issue. Water was available on board. headsets were available on board, to reduce flight noise and hear the pilot clearly.

This is a single prop plane, with 'just right' speed to enjoy the sights. It does not fly low or close to attractions nor make much changes in elevation while in flight, like helicopters can. IMHO this lets you get a grand view of the attractions, which is what is ride is about.

Landing was safe and well executed. Getting off the plane was simple and quick.

Review Text:
Aside from the opportunity to soak in some gorgeous and dramatic views of the island, the whole-island tour was an especially enjoyable trip for a pilot. I had originally wanted to fly in their C182, a private 4-seat Cessna, with an instructor, because it is the only way to fly around the island, at the controls, unless you take a checkout flight so you can rent further, solo (more of an option for residents). My wife and I decided this time to take the tour in the AirVan, with J.T. as our pilot and tour guide, along with a few other passengers.

Even though we pilots are always itching to be at the controls, this was still a fine choice. The airspace is relatively busy with other air tours and traffic, there are several local VFR reference points you don’t know, and the terrain has unique properties which require attention, as well. I was simply able to sit back and enjoy the beauty of Kauai—without getting too antsy to fly, myself!

Incidentally, with the varying terrain and ocean comes what’s called “uneven heating” which is one of the factors which creates turbulence. There’s only two things one can do to mitigate that: 1) fly early in the morning, or 2) get a pilot who knows how to soften the ride (there are a few ways). J.T. is just such a pilot.

Highly recommend! (20 year, instrument pilot)

Review Text:
Our photography flight with Air Ventures—the most eco-friendly air tour company in Kauai—was one of the highlights of our Hawaiian adventure. Owner Jill Briley and her outgoing staff ensured that everything was air-tight prior to takeoff. With over 8,000 hours of flight time and a sparkling personality, Captain Eric ensured that we were safe and entertained from takeoff to landing.

Soaring over Kauai was a truly amazing experience. We covered a lot of ground from the air—the entire Garden Island—in just over an hour with the Big Kahuna tour.

The most epic highlights on an island of breathtaking coastlines were Waita Reservoir (the largest on Kauai), Captain Cook’s Landing, the inspiring Waimea Canyon, the surreal Napali Coastline, Lumahai Beach (where “South Pacific” was filmed), Hanalei Valley, countless beautiful cascading waterfalls and the Kilauea Lighthouse. It is so beautiful that over 60 movies have been filmed here, including Blue Hawaii, King Kong, Jurassic Park, Soul Surfer, The Descendants and Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides.

Review Text:
I had never been in a small craft before, so I was scared and relictant even as I buckled in while still on the tarmac. Even after the smooth take-off, and cruise past landmarks, I still expected the plane to buck and pitch and to cause me to use the air-sickness bag. However, none of the former or latter happened. Our pilot, Eric, with his 30 years of flying expertise, flew that plane rock steady. His calm demeanor, seemingly effortless flying, and his abundant knowledge of the island distracted my mind from my unfounded fears of a plane-crash death.
As for the sights, we were able to see most of the must-see places all over the island. The views were so good in fact, that we didn’t even feel the need to see them up close anymore. Why go to the (Fantasy Island) waterfalls by car just to see it from the freeway, when we’ve already seen it from the best angle available? The same went for spouting horn and other attractions. We even saw sea turtles from our vantage point in the air.
But what goes up must come down. Again, Captain Eric did not disappoint. The landing was so smooth I didn’t even feel the moment when the wheels actually touched the ground.
All in all a great flight. I highly recommend it!!

We kept our time slot and showed up early. There were seven of us scheduled to fly together, everyone amiable and sharing their travel stories. The flight lasted almost an hour - and we saw EVERYTHING. Also, when I asked the pilot to show us something specifically, he nodded and made sure to include it along our route, even doubling back a few miles to point out the open-air cave along the Na Pali Coast.

When we returned, we spoke to a man from our hotel who paid twice as much to go on a helicopter ride for half the time and saw a third of what we saw (and if I haven't mentioned it, we saw the entire island). His wife was none too pleased at being left behind, and he said the helicopter ride was incredibly bumpy - hard to photograph. My photographs came out spectacular.

I got an incredibly great price on this, and I think Air Ventures would lose money if everyone found the coupon I did. But if you're on a budget and enjoy star treatment, do your research ahead of time and expect to be rewarded.

One of the girls on the right side was kind enough to snap a few pictures for me and also thought it was foolish how they arranged us. The rest of the trip consisted of me sticking my arm over to where the tot was and trying to get pics and then finally shutting my camera off and giving up. The waterfall was the only thing the pilot circled back for, for me to see. I missed the entire Napali Coast which was the main thing I wanted to see. Oh there is Julia Roberts house and there is Pierce Brosnan's place. (The tot does not know who they are.) I will never know with my view of the ocean, wing, and white bar holding the wing on. This was absolute crap. Do yourself a favor and wait until you are here and book a helicopter tour. I have been sick at my stomach all day from this tiny plane and also just feel very ripped off. I cannot believe the pilot gave a tot a cherry seat and stuck me where he did either. A short girl getting to spread out in front. I had a 20 dollar tip ready but I left tipping nothing. I guess I will go blow 15 on a beer at the St. Regis where I am staying. Did not like the reference that it was foolish to spend 15 on a beer. What was foolish was this plane ride. I think I should get refunded as I have booked a copter tour tomorrow and have to drive all the way back to that side of the island to get a decent tour. The place I went to book another tour right after this said I would get a seat I wanted. They said they did not think that was right giving two of three people in a group, especially a little kid the good seats. They thought I probably only paid 60-70 though. Oh boy, I paid much more and got to watch a family make great memories while I sat in the worst seat on the plane. Not as advertised. Avoid at all costs! What a waste of a day and now I have to drive out of my way again for a decent tour. If you can't tell I am writing this while I am still mad. Just terrible. As if all this is not bad enough if you are on the right side, the plane still flies very very high. Not up close and personal at all like it was made out to be.

Review Title: Best Way to View the Entire Island
Review Text:
We did this on our third day and really were glad that we did. We did the 1-hour tour and got the free DVD for booking online. (By the way, the DVD is worth it if you book online and get it for free, but not for the $20 or whatever you had to pay for it, it's only like 20 min. long and doesn't have that great of quality, but was a nice gift for us since it was free!) This was something my husband was adamant about doing and since I get really motion sick, I wasn't originally too keen on it. In fact, he originally started wanting to do a doors-off helicopter ride and I was excited to find Air Ventures had such great reviews so that I could suggest this as an alternative to the helicopter, which went over well and I think he's very happy that we did it this way.

You really get to see the entire island from above and get some of the history from your guide. Our guide/pilot wasn't as talkative as we would have liked, but really no one on the plane was asking questions or talking to him either, so I think it's understandable that it turned out that way. And most of the sights speak for themselves. You get to see the coffee fields, all of the fabulous/famous beaches of the island, waterfalls, Waimea Canyon, where Jurassic Park/Raiders of the Lost Ark was filmed, etc etc etc --- it is really all encompassing and I would recommend it.

The people that run it and were the pilots were SUPER nice as well, which really makes for an awesome trip, especially because I was a little nervous about flying in such a small plane.

As for the motion sickness, I did ok for a half hour and then was feeling really ill for the second half, but I never actually got sick and imagine it's MUCH better than a helicopter ride would have been. And they were very sweet about it as well, offering watering and where I could sit to cool off, so that was much appreciated.

I think this is a must do for those on Kauai, it's so cool to see all of the places from above and then spend the rest of the week exploring from the ground or water, very cool!

Review Text: Yesterday my wife, a friend, and I went on a flight over Kauai riding in a fixed wing aircraft flown by an experienced pilot from Air Ventures.  We debated flying in a helicopter instead of the fixed wing aircraft, because a helicopter can hover over a scenic location, but opted for the lower cost aircraft.  We had heard that the Air Van aircraft, which seats 7 passengers and flies at about 115 - 120 mph offers plenty of time to take pictures of waterfalls and other scenic spots.  Each passenger is seated next to an optically clear plastic window and is provided an opportunity to photograph locations of interest.  I was using my new digital SLR and got some great photos.  The flight takes an hour and the plane travels (at least our flight did) in a clockwise direction around the island, primarily along the coast line and over the Waimea Canyon (the Grand Canyon of the Pacific), traveling over the Hanalei Valley when returning to Lihue.  My wife and I had toured much of the island by vehicle on a trip to Kauai with two other friends just last January, but seeing the canyon and some of the waterfalls that we had seen from the road-side access was not nearly as exciting as the view from the aircraft.  We particularly enjoyed flying over the Napali coast (western shoreline) and seeing all of the waterfalls.  Our flight was on a relatively clear day after several days of intermittent heavy rainfall, so the waterfalls were spectacular and abundant.  The pilot was very good about pointing out the sites and telling us historical anecdotes about various scenic locations.  The noise-canceling headphones and microphones provided each passenger enabled us to hear him clearly and ask questions.  He was an excellent pilot, considerate about minimizing turbulence by flying above it or moving away from the cliffs, and very knowledgeable about Kauai.  In short, I would strongly recommend taking the Air Ventures aircraft flight as providing one of the best ways to see all of the major sites of interest on the entire island.  We all enjoyed the flight and felt it provided more than any other recreational experience during this vacation.

Review Title: See Kauai from the air with Air Ventures
Review Text:
Flying with Air Ventures is not just a cheaper alternative to taking the more expensive helicopter tours!

You get a full hour tour with a great guide and pilot (Joel) to tour all of the major sights of the island and see things you cannot see from the ground.

The plane is specially designed for low speed flying and much quieter than the helicopters. You get a headset and microphone to enable two way communication with the pilot.

You will see the harbor, the entire western coast (NaPali), Kalalau Valley, Hanalei Bay, Princeville, numerous waterfalls, the Powerline Trail, Mt. Waialeale, coffee plantations, Wailua Falls, and many other sights.

This was our fourth trip to Kauai but our first time to see the island from the air and it is well worth the money spent. Don't book with any other airplane or helicopter tour. Then report your experiences back to this website!
